the Hunnic kings. In the month of Haziran of this same year,
the accursed Kurds lay in ambush on Mount Alphaph,
and captured ten monks from the monastery of Mor Mattai,
and tortured them;
and one of them, who was surnamed Matsutha, they killed;
and the other nine they sold for four thousand zuzas.
And in the year one thousand five hundred and eighty-nine [1278 AD],
1589. King Leon sent,
and took his daughter, who was the daughter-in-law of the Parwana, to himself,
because her husband had been carried off to Egypt,
as we have said.
And in this same year,
there was a severe winter and intense cold in Azerbaijan and in all Greater Armenia as far as the border of the Scythians;
and the horses, cattle, and sheep of all the tent-dwellers perished.
And there was a very great shortage of food,
for a hundred minas of wheat, that is, a small donkey-load, was sold in Mughan for forty Rukni dinars.
And in this winter, Papa (Baba?) the Persian,
he whom Mas'ud bar Qawti had deposed from the governorship of Mosul,
calumniated Mas'ud, saying that he was destroying the country of Mosul,
and did not know how to govern.
Then the King of Kings ordered certain great nobles,
and they came with Papa (with Baba?) to Mosul.
And that Papa (Baba?) set up false witnesses against Ashmut and Mas'ud,
and he also bribed the judges, and they perverted justice,
and condemned those Christians,
and deposed them,
and gave authority to Papa (to Baba?).
And in the summer of this year, a multitude of Turkmens, Bedouins, and collected Kurds who were in Syria gathered together,
and entered Cilicia,
and reached as far as Tall Hamdun,
and wrought great destruction in that country;
and when they had taken much plunder, they departed.
And in the year one thousand five hundred and ninety [1279 AD],
the Christians [cancelled] their procession on the Day of the Epiphany to bless the waters over the river,
on account of a riot which the Arabs had stirred up with them,
[and because] the cold was severe,
[she] came in person to the city of Maraghah,
and commanded the Christians to go out,
according to their custom,
with crosses hung upon the heads of spears.
And when they went out,
divine grace visited them,
and the intensity of the frost was subdued,
and the grass flourished.
